title: Token stewardship framework for service and personal keys
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Tokens (API keys, service tokens, and session tokens) are proliferating with inconsistent metadata, naming, and expiry handling. That creates blind spots in audits, complicates emergency revocation, and prevents safe automation for rotation. Goal: Design and implement a Token Stewardship Framework that standardizes token metadata, enforces per-scope tokens, automates rotation/expiry, and integrates with RBAC v2 and audit logging so operators can reliably discover, revoke, and reason about credentials.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Every issued token type (service, personal, ephemeral) has a canonical metadata envelope (name, owner principal, scope tags, environment, created_by, expires_at, rotation_policy_id). 2) All new token creation paths populate the envelope; existing tokens are discoverable and backfilled within a migration window. 3) Rotation automation can schedule and rotate tokens for eligible token classes without breaking bound deployments (graceful rollout). 4) Audit logs record token events (create, rotate, revoke, backfill) with principal and request context and are queryable by token id and owner. 5) Admin console surfaces token inventory, orphan detection, and emergency revoke controls.
technical_notes:
- Introduce a canonical token metadata schema stored in credentials service (k/v) and surfaced in audit events.
- Add token-tagging middleware in token minting endpoints (API, Console, CLI, SSO-provisioner).
- Distinguish token classes: service-long (for reserved infra), service-ephemeral (for workloads with short TTL), user-api (personal keys), and session (SSO-backed).
- Integrate with RBAC v2: tokens inherit principal's role binding unless explicitly bound to a service account with explicit scope tags.
- Store rotation_policy objects referenced by tokens rather than per-token config to enable policy updates.
- Use existing credential-ledger APIs (refactor idempotency and audit hooks) and extend audit schema with token_id and metadata snapshot.
implementation_steps: 1. Schema design: finalize canonical envelope and rotation_policy schema (security sign-off). 2. Minting paths: add middleware to API and Console token creation to populate metadata and assign rotation_policy_id. 3. Backfill job: read legacy tokens, attempt owner resolution, tag as backfilled, and surface to console. 4. Rotation engine: add scheduler that enqueues rotations, performs canary rotate for dependent services, and records audit events. 5. Emergency revoke API + Console flow. 6. RBAC v2 mapping: ensure token issuance checks role bindings and attaches immutable scope tags. 7. Observability: add metrics (tokens_total_by_class, tokens_rotations_success, tokens_orphans_count) and dashboards. 8. Create migration runbook and monitoring alerts.
rollout_plan: Phase A (0-2 weeks): Schema and API changes behind feature flag; no user-facing changes. Phase B (2-5 weeks): Enable minting middleware and rotation_policy creation; run backfill in read-only mode to surface issues. Phase C (5-8 weeks): Start automated rotation for non-critical service-ephemeral tokens with canary groups; enable console inventory UI. Phase D (>8 weeks): Expand rotation to user-api tokens with gradual enforcement and opt-out for grandfathered tokens; enforce naming/expiry on new tokens. Emergency-revoke runs & drills scheduled during low-traffic windows.
qa_steps:
- Unit tests for schema validation and middleware.
- Integration tests that simulate token creation across API/Console/SSO flows and validate audit events.
- End-to-end rotation test: create a service token, perform canary rotate, verify client rebind and success metrics.
- Backfill dry-run verifying owner resolution heuristics and sampling manual review.
- Pen-test checklist: replay audit events, attempt privilege escalation via token reuse.
- Load test: ensure token ledger queries scale with inventory size (target 500k tokens).
